programme.subtitle: Build a VPC, managed Amazon EKS cluster, node group, container image, and Kubernetes application from scratch
programme.description: Kubernetes is software for running and managing containerized applications. A container packages an application and its dependencies into a portable image. A Kubernetes cluster is the environment that runs those containers. In Amazon EKS, AWS manages the Kubernetes control plane—the API endpoint and components that keep track of the desired state—while worker nodes are Amazon EC2 instances that run application workloads. A Pod is the smallest deployable Kubernetes unit and normally contains one application container. A Deployment declares a desired number of identical Pods; Kubernetes creates ReplicaSets to maintain that number and replaces failed Pods. A Service provides a stable network name and virtual IP for matching Pods selected by labels. A Namespace is a logical workspace inside a cluster. Labels are key-value metadata used to select and organize resources. Desired state means you declare what should exist, and Kubernetes continuously reconciles actual state back to that declaration. This lab uses a private managed node group in two Availability Zones, a public Network Load Balancer created by a Kubernetes LoadBalancer Service, Amazon ECR for the learner-built nginx image, IAM roles for EKS and nodes, VPC routing, and CloudWatch-backed EKS control-plane logging.
programme.learningOutcome: Create, operate, troubleshoot, and delete a complete beginner EKS environment without relying on existing AWS or Kubernetes infrastructure.

tasks.title: Learn the vocabulary, install tools, and create the dedicated training identity
tasks.feature: Kubernetes foundations, IAM, AWS CLI, kubectl, and eksctl
tasks.goal: Prepare one safe training identity and the command-line tools required to create and administer the lab.
tasks.whyItMatters: The AWS account root user has unrestricted access. AWS recommends using root only for tasks that require it and not creating root access keys. This temporary lab uses one dedicated IAM user only because the exercise requires a named local CLI profile; production human access should prefer federation and temporary credentials.

consoleSteps.title: Protect the account root user

instructions.text: Enable MFA for the root user if it is not already enabled.
Do not create a root access key.
Sign in as an existing administrator.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Root access is protected and an administrator, rather than root, performs routine lab setup.
consoleSteps.warning: Stop if you only have root access and cannot safely enable MFA.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training user and console sign-in

instructions.text: Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console.
Select I want to create an IAM user.
Select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Record the Console sign-in URL as [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The account contains fa-eks-beginner-user and [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] identifies its sign-in page.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not share the password or sign-in URL with untrusted people.

consoleSteps.title: Create and attach the training policy

instructions.text: Replace the policy editor contents with the copyable policy JSON.
Replace every occurrence of [ACCOUNT_ID] with the 12-digit AWS account ID shown in the top-right account menu.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-eks-beginner-user has the dedicated lab policy. The policy permits this short-lived lab but is broader than a production policy.
consoleSteps.warning: The policy intentionally permits only named lab IAM resources for mutable IAM actions and is deleted during cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Create programmatic credentials and configure the profile

instructions.text: Store the downloaded file only long enough to run aws configure.
Delete the downloaded file after configuration.
Enter the downloaded access key ID when prompted.
Enter the downloaded secret access key when prompted.
Enter eu-west-2 for Default region name.
Enter json for Default output format.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The local AWS CLI profile named fa-eks-beginner is configured for Europe (London).
consoleSteps.warning: The secret access key is displayed only once. Never put it in a command, source file, YAML, screenshot, shell history, or notes.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: confirm that AWS CLI version 2 is installed before configuring the profile.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output begins with aws-cli/2.
cliSteps.warning: Install AWS CLI version 2 from the official installer if this command is unavailable.

cliSteps.expectedResult: The output includes Client Version.
cliSteps.warning: Do not connect kubectl to a cluster until the cluster exists.

cliSteps.explanation: eksctl command: confirm that eksctl is installed. This lab uses AWS CLI for explicit resource creation and eksctl for an independent cluster-status check.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output includes an eksctl version.
cliSteps.warning: Use an up-to-date eksctl release supported by the EKS documentation.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: run once as an existing administrator. <ADMIN_PROFILE> is the administrator profile, not the training profile that does not exist yet.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains UserName fa-eks-beginner-user.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run with root access keys.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: first create a local file named fa-eks-beginner-policy.json containing the exact policy JSON in the Console JSON block after replacing [ACCOUNT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the ARN for fa-eks-beginner-policy.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so this command intentionally has no --region.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the account ID used in the policy document.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The policy is attached to fa-eks-beginner-user.
cliSteps.warning: IAM permission changes can take a short time to propagate.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: immediately enter the returned access key ID and secret access key into the next interactive aws configure command; record only the returned AccessKeyId as [IAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID] for cleanup.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an AccessKeyId and one-time SecretAccessKey.
cliSteps.warning: Do not copy the secret access key into any file or chat. Delete the access key during final cleanup.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: enter the new training-user access key, its secret, eu-west-2, and json at the prompts.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local profile is created in the AWS shared credentials and config files.
cliSteps.warning: This interactive command stores long-term credentials locally; remove the profile during cleanup.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: verify the active caller before creating regional resources.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Arn identifies fa-eks-beginner-user and the Account value is the intended account.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated two-AZ VPC and EKS subnet tags
tasks.goal: Create public and private subnets, an internet gateway, one cost-conscious NAT gateway, route tables, and the EKS subnet tags required for public load balancing.
tasks.whyItMatters: EKS needs at least two subnets. Private node subnets use the NAT gateway for outbound image pulls and package access. Public subnets are used by the internet-facing Kubernetes LoadBalancer Service. A single NAT gateway reduces lab cost but is not a production high-availability design.

consoleSteps.title: Create the VPC and four subnets

instructions.text: Enter 10.60.0.0/24 in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Enter 10.60.1.0/24 in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Enter 10.60.10.0/24 in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Enter 10.60.11.0/24 in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Record each Subnet ID from the Subnets list as [PUBLIC_A_ID], [PUBLIC_B_ID], [PRIVATE_A_ID], and [PRIVATE_B_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A dedicated VPC has two public and two private subnets across eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use the default VPC for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Create public and private routing

instructions.text: Select [NAT_EIP_ALLOCATION_ID] in Elastic IP allocation ID.
Wait for State to become Available.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Public subnets route through the internet gateway; private subnets route outbound traffic through the NAT gateway.
consoleSteps.warning: NAT gateways and Elastic IP addresses can incur charges. Delete them promptly in the final phase.

consoleSteps.title: Add EKS and load-balancer subnet tags

instructions.text: Repeat the public-subnet tags for fa-eks-beginner-public-b.
Repeat the private-subnet tags for fa-eks-beginner-private-b.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: EKS can identify cluster subnets, public subnets can host internet-facing load balancers, and private subnets can host internal load balancers.
consoleSteps.warning: Tags are AWS metadata. Kubernetes labels and annotations are separate concepts.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record the returned VpcId as [VPC_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The VPC is created with CIDR 10.60.0.0/16.
cliSteps.warning: Use only [VPC_ID] returned by this lab.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.60.0.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-eks-beginner-public-a}] --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record SubnetId as [PUBLIC_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The first public subnet exists.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the earlier create-vpc result.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.60.1.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-eks-beginner-public-b}] --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record SubnetId as [PUBLIC_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The second public subnet exists.
cliSteps.warning: Use a different Availability Zone from public-a.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.60.10.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-eks-beginner-private-a}] --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record SubnetId as [PRIVATE_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The first private subnet exists.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet receives its default route through the NAT gateway later.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.60.11.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-eks-beginner-private-b}] --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record SubnetId as [PRIVATE_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The second private subnet exists.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet receives its default route through the NAT gateway later.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record InternetGatewayId as [IGW_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The internet gateway is created.
cliSteps.warning: Attach it only to [VPC_ID].

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: attach the gateway to the dedicated VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The internet gateway is attached.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders with values created in this lab.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record RouteTableId as [PUBLIC_RT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public route table is created.
cliSteps.warning: Associate only public subnets with it.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: add the public IPv4 default route.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public route table has a default route to the internet gateway.
cliSteps.warning: Do not add this route to the private route table.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record AllocationId as [NAT_EIP_ALLOCATION_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: An Elastic IP allocation is returned.
cliSteps.warning: An unassociated Elastic IP can incur charges.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record NatGatewayId as [NAT_GATEWAY_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The NAT gateway begins creating.
cliSteps.warning: Wait until it is Available before creating the private default route.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record RouteTableId as [PRIVATE_RT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The private route table is created.
cliSteps.warning: Use it only for the two private node subnets.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: add outbound-only IPv4 routing for private nodes.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The private route table has a default route to the NAT gateway.
cliSteps.warning: The NAT gateway must be Available.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: associate public subnet A.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A route-table association ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Repeat the matching operation for public subnet B.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: associate public subnet B.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A route-table association ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Use [PUBLIC_RT_ID].

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: associate private subnet A.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A route-table association ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Use [PRIVATE_RT_ID].

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: associate private subnet B.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A route-table association ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Use [PRIVATE_RT_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-tags --resources [PUBLIC_A_ID] [PUBLIC_B_ID] --tags Key=kubernetes.io/cluster/fa-eks-beginner-cluster,Value=shared Key=kubernetes.io/role/elb,Value=1 --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: tag both public subnets for this cluster and public load balancers.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public subnet tags are created.
cliSteps.warning: Do not apply the public elb tag to private subnets.

cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: tag both private subnets for this cluster and internal load balancers.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The private subnet tags are created.
cliSteps.warning: Do not apply the internal-elb tag to public subnets.

verification.instruction: Inspect the public and private route tables in the VPC console.
verification.expectedResult: The public table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW and the private table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway.

verification.title: Verify two-AZ EKS tags

tasks.title: Create separate IAM roles for the EKS control plane and managed nodes
tasks.goal: Create fa-eks-beginner-cluster-role and fa-eks-beginner-node-role with their documented AWS managed policies.
tasks.whyItMatters: The control plane role lets EKS manage AWS resources for the cluster. The node role lets kubelet, Amazon VPC CNI, and nodes obtain required AWS permissions. AWS documentation states that the node role must not be the same role used to create the cluster.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EKS cluster role

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable EKS cluster trust policy JSON for the CLI route

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The cluster role trusts eks.amazonaws.com and has AmazonEKSClusterPolicy attached.

consoleSteps.title: Create the managed node role

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable EC2 node trust policy JSON for the CLI route

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The node role trusts ec2.amazonaws.com and has the WorkerNode, CNI, and ECR pull-only managed policies.

tasks.title: Create the EKS control plane
tasks.goal: Create fa-eks-beginner-cluster in eu-west-2 using the dedicated VPC and all four subnets.
tasks.whyItMatters: Amazon EKS creates and manages the Kubernetes control plane. The cluster creator gains Kubernetes administrative access, so all later kubectl commands must use the same fa-eks-beginner-user profile.

consoleSteps.title: Create the cluster

instructions.text: Turn Use EKS Auto Mode off.
Select fa-eks-beginner-cluster-role in Cluster IAM role.
Leave Bootstrap cluster administrator access enabled.
Select IPv4 for Cluster IP address family.
Leave the public cluster endpoint enabled for this temporary beginner lab.
Leave the default Amazon VPC CNI, CoreDNS, and kube-proxy add-ons selected.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-eks-beginner-cluster becomes Active and the EKS-created cluster security group ID is recorded.
consoleSteps.warning: An EKS cluster is chargeable while it exists. The public endpoint is convenient for a short beginner lab; production endpoint access needs a deliberate security design.

cliSteps.command: aws eks create-cluster --name fa-eks-beginner-cluster --role-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/fa-eks-beginner-cluster-role --resources-vpc-config subnetIds=[PUBLIC_A_ID],[PUBLIC_B_ID],[PRIVATE_A_ID],[PRIVATE_B_ID],endpointPublicAccess=true,endpointPrivateAccess=true --kubernetes-network-config ipFamily=ipv4 --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the same account ID used earlier and replace each subnet placeholder with the recorded IDs. AWS creates a cluster security group automatically.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows cluster status CREATING.
cliSteps.warning: This creates a chargeable EKS control plane. Do not continue to node creation until status is ACTIVE.

cliSteps.command: aws eks wait cluster-active --name fa-eks-beginner-cluster --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: wait for the EKS API to report the cluster as active.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits without an error.
cliSteps.warning: Cluster creation can take several minutes.

cliSteps.command: aws eks describe-cluster --name fa-eks-beginner-cluster --query cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId --output text --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: AWS CLI command: record the output as [EKS_CLUSTER_SECURITY_GROUP_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output is an sg- security group ID created by EKS.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete or alter this security group while the cluster exists.

verification.title: Verify cluster state
verification.instruction: Open the EKS cluster Overview tab or run describe-cluster.
verification.expectedResult: Status is Active and the cluster VPC is fa-eks-beginner-vpc.

verification.title: Explain the control-plane security group

verification.expectedResult: The learner understands that EKS creates the cluster security group and deletes it with the cluster when no longer needed.

tasks.title: Create private managed nodes, ECR repository, and the application image
tasks.feature: Managed node groups and Amazon ECR
tasks.goal: Create a small managed node group, a private ECR repository, and two learner-built nginx image versions.
tasks.whyItMatters: Managed node groups create EC2 worker nodes that register with the cluster. The application image is stored in the learner-owned ECR repository, so the deployment does not assume a pre-existing application image. Versioned images make rolling update and rollback observable.

consoleSteps.title: Create the managed node group

instructions.text: Select fa-eks-beginner-node-role in Node IAM role.
Leave Configure SSH access to nodes disabled.
Wait until node-group Status shows Active.

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable Dockerfile for ECR image version v1
jsonBlocks.content:
FROM nginx:1.27 RUN printf '

fa-eks-nginx version v1

Amazon EKS beginner lab

\n' > /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A private, on-demand t3.small managed node group is Active with one desired node and capacity to scale to two.
consoleSteps.warning: Managed nodes are chargeable EC2 instances. One desired node is cost-conscious but is not highly available.

consoleSteps.title: Create the ECR repository

instructions.text: Leave Mutable selected for Image tag mutability.
Use the displayed Region eu-west-2 repository URI when tagging the image.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The private repository exists and [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI] is available for the deployment manifest.
consoleSteps.warning: ECR image storage can incur charges. The node role has ECR pull-only access, while the training user policy permits the push actions.

consoleSteps.title: Build and push image v1 from the console route
consoleSteps.instruction: Open AWS CloudShell from the console toolbar.

instructions.text: Open AWS CloudShell from the console toolbar.
Create a local folder named fa-eks-nginx-v1.
Create a file named Dockerfile in that folder.
Paste the version v1 Dockerfile JSON-block text into Dockerfile.
Run the individual AWS CLI and Docker commands from this task in CloudShell.
Use [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI] as the image repository value.
Verify that tag v1 appears on the ECR Images tab.

tasks.title: Connect kubectl and deploy the namespace, Deployment, and ClusterIP Service
tasks.feature: kubectl connection and core Kubernetes objects
tasks.goal: Write kubeconfig, verify the current Kubernetes context, create fa-eks-lab, deploy nginx from ECR, and provide an internal ClusterIP Service.
tasks.whyItMatters: kubeconfig connects kubectl to the EKS API. The Deployment declares two desired replicas, the ReplicaSet maintains them, and the ClusterIP Service gives selected Pods an internal stable endpoint without creating an AWS load balancer.

consoleSteps.title: Connect from the EKS console
consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudShell opens with kubectl configured for fa-eks-beginner-cluster and at least one node is visible.
consoleSteps.warning: The cluster creator identity is the Kubernetes administrator for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Create the namespace and internal application resources
consoleSteps.instruction: In CloudShell, create a local file named fa-eks-nginx-internal.yaml.

instructions.text: In CloudShell, create a local file named fa-eks-nginx-internal.yaml.
Paste the complete YAML JSON-block content into the file.
Replace [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI] with the URI recorded from the ECR repository page.

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable fa-eks-nginx-internal.yaml
jsonBlocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-lab
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-nginx
  namespace: fa-eks-lab
  labels:
    app: fa-eks-nginx
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fa-eks-nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fa-eks-nginx
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI]:v1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "50m"
              memory: "64Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "250m"
              memory: "128Mi"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-nginx-clusterip
  namespace: fa-eks-lab
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: fa-eks-nginx
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The fa-eks-lab namespace contains a Deployment with two desired replicas and an internal ClusterIP Service.
consoleSteps.warning: A ClusterIP Service is reachable only inside the cluster unless another resource forwards traffic to it.

tasks.title: Expose nginx with a public LoadBalancer Service
tasks.feature: Kubernetes Service and Elastic Load Balancing
tasks.goal: Create fa-eks-nginx-public as an internet-facing LoadBalancer Service, record its endpoint, and test it.
tasks.whyItMatters: ClusterIP keeps traffic inside the cluster. LoadBalancer asks the AWS cloud integration to create an Elastic Load Balancing resource. For this lab, the public-subnet tags and service annotations request an internet-facing Network Load Balancer.

consoleSteps.title: Create and inspect the public service from CloudShell

instructions.text: Create a local file named fa-eks-nginx-public.yaml.
Paste the complete LoadBalancer Service YAML JSON-block content into the file.
Record the EXTERNAL-IP hostname as [LOADBALANCER_HOSTNAME] when it appears.
Press Ctrl+C to stop watch mode.
Find the load balancer whose DNS name matches [LOADBALANCER_HOSTNAME].

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable fa-eks-nginx-public.yaml
jsonBlocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-nginx-public
  namespace: fa-eks-lab
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: "internet-facing"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type: "instance"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: fa-eks-nginx
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Service receives an external DNS hostname and AWS creates the associated Network Load Balancer.
consoleSteps.warning: A LoadBalancer Service creates chargeable Elastic Load Balancing resources. Delete this Service before deleting the EKS cluster.

tasks.title: Scale, update, roll back, and consume ConfigMap and Secret data
tasks.feature: Deployments, rolling updates, ConfigMaps, and Secrets
tasks.goal: Scale the Deployment, push version v2, perform a rolling update and safe rollback, then inject non-sensitive configuration and a demonstration Secret.
tasks.whyItMatters: A Deployment maintains desired replica count and supports controlled rollout history. ConfigMaps carry non-secret configuration. Kubernetes Secrets are encoded objects, not automatically equivalent to a full secret-management design; real credentials need restricted access, encryption, rotation, and an appropriate secret-management service.

consoleSteps.title: Build and push image v2
consoleSteps.instruction: Open AWS CloudShell from the console toolbar.

instructions.text: Open AWS CloudShell from the console toolbar.
Create a local folder named fa-eks-nginx-v2.
Create a file named Dockerfile in that folder.
Paste the version v2 Dockerfile JSON-block text into Dockerfile.
Run the separate Docker build, tag, and push commands in this task.
Verify tag v2 on the ECR repository Images tab.

jsonBlocks.title: Copyable Dockerfile for ECR image version v2

FROM nginx:1.28 RUN printf '

fa-eks-nginx version v2

Rolling update demonstration

\n' > /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html

instructions.text: Create a local file named fa-eks-nginx-settings.yaml.
Paste the ConfigMap and Secret YAML JSON-block content into the file.
Run kubectl set env deployment/fa-eks-nginx --from=configmap/fa-eks-nginx-config -n fa-eks-lab.
Run kubectl set env deployment/fa-eks-nginx --from=secret/fa-eks-nginx-demo-secret -n fa-eks-lab.
Run kubectl rollout status deployment/fa-eks-nginx -n fa-eks-lab.

jsonBlocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-nginx-config
  namespace: fa-eks-lab

  LAB_GREETING: "Hello from ConfigMap"
  APP_MODE: "training"
---

kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: fa-eks-nginx-demo-secret
  namespace: fa-eks-lab
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DEMO_TOKEN: "training-only-not-a-real-secret"

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ConfigMap and demonstration Secret exist, and restarted Pods receive their key-value pairs as environment variables.
consoleSteps.warning: Never store real passwords, API keys, or private keys in this demonstration Secret. The fixed value is intentionally non-sensitive.

cliSteps.explanation: Docker command: run from the folder containing the exact v2 Dockerfile shown in this task.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A local v2 image is built.
cliSteps.warning: Build only after Docker authentication and ECR repository creation completed earlier.

cliSteps.explanation: Docker command: apply the ECR repository tag to the local v2 image.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local image is tagged for ECR.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI] with the earlier recorded URI.

cliSteps.explanation: Docker command: push v2 into the existing ECR repository.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The v2 image digest appears in ECR.
cliSteps.warning: If authentication has expired, repeat the separate ECR login commands from Task 5.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: increase the declared desired state from two to three Pods.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Deployment creates a third replica.
cliSteps.warning: A single t3.small node might have limited capacity; if a Pod stays Pending, inspect kubectl describe pod output.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: return the desired state to two Pods.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Deployment removes one replica while maintaining two available Pods.
cliSteps.warning: This confirms that desired replica count is declarative and adjustable.

cliSteps.command: kubectl set image deployment/fa-eks-nginx nginx=[ECR_REPOSITORY_URI]:v2 -n fa-eks-lab
cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: change the Deployment container image to the pushed v2 image and begin a rolling update.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Deployment records a new revision.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [ECR_REPOSITORY_URI] exactly; an invalid URI produces image-pull failures.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: wait for the rolling update to finish.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output reports that the Deployment successfully rolled out.

cliSteps.expectedResult: At least two revisions are shown: v1 and v2.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: safely return the Deployment to the prior working revision.

cliSteps.warning: Confirm rollout status after undo; rollback is not instantaneous.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: create the ConfigMap and intentionally non-sensitive Secret using the complete YAML shown in this task.
cliSteps.expectedResult: configmap/fa-eks-nginx-config and secret/fa-eks-nginx-demo-secret are created.
cliSteps.warning: The demonstration Secret value must never be changed to a real credential.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: consume ConfigMap keys as container environment variables and trigger a new rollout.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Deployment template includes ConfigMap-derived environment values.
cliSteps.warning: ConfigMap values are configuration, not secrets.

cliSteps.explanation: kubectl command: consume the demonstration Secret key as a container environment variable and trigger a new rollout.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Deployment template includes DEMO_TOKEN from the Secret.
cliSteps.warning: Do not print or log secret values in a real workload.

verification.expectedResult: The rollout completes and the page returns to the v1 content after rollback.

instructions.text: Inspect available control-plane log and metric links.

The local AWS CLI has no documented profile-delete operation equivalent to removing a profile section. The final cleanup supplies a safe manual removal route and a one-command credential blanking step; manually remove both profile sections to make the profile absent.

The EKS-created cluster security group is generated with a unique ID. Its stable recorded placeholder is [EKS_CLUSTER_SECURITY_GROUP_ID]; it is removed as part of EKS cluster deletion rather than directly while the cluster exists.

The final cleanup uses recorded route-table association placeholders [PUBLIC_A_ASSOCIATION_ID], [PUBLIC_B_ASSOCIATION_ID], [PRIVATE_A_ASSOCIATION_ID], and [PRIVATE_B_ASSOCIATION_ID]. Record each association ID from the output of its aws ec2 associate-route-table command before cleanup.

The internet gateway requires a separate aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway command after the listed detach command. The finalCleanup schema permits one CLI command per resource entry, so the Console route contains both actions and the required second CLI action should be run manually after successful detach: aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id [IGW_ID] --profile fa-eks-beginner --region eu-west-2.
